title: Independent geographic database cells
context: A record or customer may be explicitly excluded from a country. A database-wide global replication policy is not sufficient for recipient-specific entitlements.
decision: Use independent CockroachDB stores per physical residency boundary. Move approved application projections between them; do not join the four lab nodes into one cross-border SQL cluster.
alternatives: One global multi-region cluster with database locality rules; a database per legal entity.
consequences: Application federation must manage retries, reauthorization, versions and cleanup. A country cell can serve multiple entities without sharing their rights. Local HA requires multiple nodes/failure domains inside each approved geography.
gate: Inspect database, broker, backup and telemetry placement; test forbidden payloads and local-cell failures.

title: Legal entity is separate from physical placement
status: Accepted design; static catalog plus isolated migration implemented
context: Thirty entities share three initial geographic stores, while residency changes may require a new country store.
decision: Keep legal entity IDs stable and resolve entity to store through a versioned directory. Owner-qualified party/relationship keys must not encode geography. Track placement versions and writer epochs separately.
alternatives: Region on each customer as the sole federation key; one physical cluster per entity.
consequences: Co-location never grants data access. The original catalog is immutable at runtime; its planner is read-only. The isolated migration has its own mutable control row.
gate: A country move preserves business IDs and denies stale routes. Implement a resilient authoritative directory before pilot.

title: Deny overrides grants and geographic eligibility
status: Accepted and implemented in fixture policies
context: A customer can permit a recipient entity but forbid the country where that entity stores data.
decision: Intersect entity eligibility, country policy, dataset/field restrictions, purpose, consent and entitlement. Explicit exclusions win. Unknown or failed OPA decisions deny the affected operation.
alternatives: Entitlement alone; country permission alone; permissive handling of missing policy.
consequences: A logically entitled recipient may receive nothing. Never send denied candidate payloads just to discover rejection remotely; record those decisions at source.
gate: Rego, browser parity and actual database tests must agree on permitted fields and forbidden destinations.

title: Minimal global party identity and scoped relationship graphs
context: Party identity may be shared across operations while relationship, holding and servicing data remain entity/policy scoped.
decision: Treat minimal party identity as a distinct eligible scope. Apply table defaults and party/relationship/holding-key restrictions to the business graph. A global ID does not imply global personal data.
alternatives: Replicate every party attribute globally; federate only whole customer documents.
consequences: Different scopes can share source rows but produce different field projections. Validate parent closure and retain owner-qualified keys.
gate: US sees only explicitly permitted party minimum; relationship and contact exclusions remain effective.

title: One local ACID business boundary
status: Accepted; Python harness implemented, Spring Boot consolidation is pilot work
context: The bank wants fewer service handoffs and coherent transactions across related business modules.
decision: Co-locate participating business modules in one regional transaction boundary where invariants require it. Commit changed rows, sovereignty effects, outbox/audit intents and idempotency receipts locally. Remote copies are asynchronous.
alternatives: A synchronous distributed transaction across regions; a transaction per former microservice boundary.
consequences: Regional service availability and latency avoid a WAN quorum on every business command. Remote projections can lag and need explicit read freshness and policy guards.
gate: Rollback must include business and outbox rows; retry must not duplicate effects. Measure the consolidated Java implementation separately.

title: Outbox now, regional CDC and durable bus later
status: Accepted; SQL polling/journal implemented, CDC/Kafka proposed
context: The thin lab must expose commit and delivery boundaries without introducing a full messaging platform.
decision: Use a transactional outbox in the federation harness and a local transactional change journal in the migration slice. Pilot evolution is regional CockroachDB CDC feeding independently budgeted durable transport such as Kafka after authorized projection.
alternatives: Application dual writes to database and bus; raw global CDC mirroring; snapshot-only migration.
consequences: The lab is easy to run but is not a CDC/broker benchmark. CDC duplicates and lacks whole-transaction ordering; preserve versions, tombstones, manifests, inboxes and target-applied checkpoints.
gate: Crash between target commit and acknowledgement, reorder events and lose transport. Never treat a source watermark alone as proof of target application.

title: OPA rules with trusted current facts
status: Accepted; local OPA calls implemented, signed distribution proposed
context: Policies must be inspectable and shared across export, import and business-read admission.
decision: Use Rego v1 and local OPA decision services. Construct policy input from trusted state. Evaluate source and recipient admission; enforce route, writer and data versions transactionally outside OPA as well.
alternatives: Ad hoc policy flags in every service; remote central policy call for every decision; trusting a previous allow event forever.
consequences: A bundle rollout is not a simultaneous authority fence. Signed rules, fact freshness, revocation leases/watermarks and rule hashes remain pilot controls.
gate: Missing/invalid decisions fail closed; stale allowed events cannot restore prohibited data.

title: Audit evidence and OpenTelemetry are distinct
status: Accepted; regional SQL audit and OTel wiring implemented
context: Sampled traces cannot provide a complete or immutable record of sovereignty decisions.
decision: Keep audit intents in the local business/control transaction and instrument flows with OpenTelemetry. Use bounded metric dimensions and regional telemetry routing; do not export customer payloads into global diagnostics.
alternatives: Use traces as the audit trail; centralize raw payload logs worldwide.
consequences: The lab's SQL audit and recent UI events are not immutable bank evidence. Regional append-only relay, retention and access controls are pilot work. The local collector uses a debug exporter.
gate: Observe Collector receipt and local traces; separately prove audit completeness, retention and no forbidden telemetry.

title: Separate authority, operational and bulk capacity
status: Accepted target design; executable queue model only
context: A broad policy change must not put historical movement ahead of fresh operational records.
decision: Reserve authority-guard and operational delivery resources; cap bulk reconciliation/migration separately. Policy activation commits scoped authority plus a cursor rather than enumerating the affected dataset.
alternatives: One FIFO worker/queue for all work; prioritize operations without separating database and I/O budgets.
consequences: Ordering cannot be assumed across lanes; current authority and data versions resolve races. The original v3 runtime still has a serial worker/global lock. The migration slice has a separate bounded entity lock, not production isolation.
gate: Run open-arrival foreground load during large reconciliation; measure p99/errors and disk contention, not only queue lengths.

title: Treat capacity results as models and targets
status: Accepted analysis method; measured database targets pending
context: Planning needs to address 50M parties and 100M relationships without implying a full-size database has been benchmarked.
decision: Keep analytic cardinality/storage, sampled queue simulations, actual OPA component timings and future service SLO targets explicitly separate. Preserve assumptions, seeds, results and validation scripts.
alternatives: Label simulated p95/p99 as production performance; provision solely by row count.
consequences: Skew, sharing density, graph size, retained history and recovery headroom can dominate. Targets are gates to measure, not promises.
gate: Replace assumptions with regional measurements; benchmark foreground tails under bulk load and failure recovery.

title: Source-writable copy followed by fenced cutover
context: Adding Mumbai should move an India entity without pausing its business operations for the entire copy.
decision: Capture a consistent snapshot and continuous changes, copy bounded batches, reconcile versions/tombstones/closure, then fence the old writer. Persist the new route as ACTIVATING before enabling the new epoch. Cleanup follows separately.
alternatives: Fence before the entire bulk copy; uncontrolled dual writer; change store_id without moving records.
consequences: A short entity-specific write pause is explicit. A new source write invalidates validation. After target writes there is no automatic route flip-back. The slice uses typed envelopes, not a migration of the normalized business.* tables; its control row remains in SG.
gate: CockroachDB cutover/restart tests plus competing-controller/partition tests before pilot. Deadline expiry cannot create an implicit policy extension.

title: Separate denial, live purge and retained-storage disposal
context: Deleting current SQL rows does not erase MVCC/WAL, backups, caches, audit or offline copies.
decision: Expose authority enforcement, live-copy cleanup and retained-surface disposal as distinct milestones. Keep durable fences after purge and quarantine restores until current policy is applied.
alternatives: Declare regulatory erasure immediately after SQL DELETE; remove fences with the payload.
consequences: COMPLETE in the migration lab means only the documented live fixture surfaces. Legal holds, encryption-key scope and backup lifecycle require separate decisions and evidence.
gate: Inventory every persistent surface, demonstrate restore fencing and record lawful deadline exceptions.

title: One node per store and one coordinator for the lab
status: Accepted lab scope; production HA explicitly excluded
context: The user requested a small development proof of concept rather than a full product deployment.
decision: Run four independent start-single-node CockroachDB containers and one API/coordinator worker. Preserve regional/service interfaces as extension points.
alternatives: A production HA fleet immediately; one shared database pretending to enforce physical geography.
consequences: Geography is a label on one host. Single-node loss causes unavailability. In-process locks do not establish distributed fencing, and no HA/physical-residency claim follows.
gate: Build pilot cells across local failure domains and validate actual placement, identity and distributed authority.

title: CockroachDB is mandatory for development deployment
status: Accepted and enforced at service entry points
context: SQLite adapter tests were useful earlier but must not masquerade as a working CockroachDB development lab.
decision: Container deployment uses CockroachDB only. Live UI mode is supplied by gateway configuration, not hostname guessing. API/dependency failure must remain visible, with no SQLite or browser-simulation fallback.
alternatives: Silently use SQLite or browser memory when the API/database fails.
consequences: Docker and working CockroachDB services are prerequisites. The explicitly selected historical SQLite unit-test adapter is retained as prior work, excluded from deployment and acceptance claims.
gate: Ready checks identify CockroachDB; tests reject alternate live modes and unavailable configuration.

title: One portable repository and verified documentation navigation
context: The monitor and supporting designs were split across two evolving projects and absolute hosted links.
decision: Consolidate source, fixtures, diagrams, design builders, ADRs, model results, tests and container helpers in one private Git repository. Build a local portal with portable links and verify referenced files/fragments and deployment claims.
alternatives: Keep separate downloads with drift; copy only rendered pages without editable source.
consequences: Generated content is reproducible. Preserve source provenance and mark historical documents. The Sites private source repository is available now; optional GitHub publishing needs an authenticated CLI.
gate: Clean rebuild, navigation/asset checks, source archive integrity and exact committed-source packaging.

title: A development gateway with explicit production boundary
context: The lab should have one entry point for UI, design pages and business/control APIs.
decision: Use an Nginx gateway bound to host loopback, serving the lab portal and proxying /api/ to the single harness. Regional authenticated business gateways remain a target deployment design.
alternatives: Expose SQL/OPA directly to the user; describe distributed gateways as already implemented.
consequences: Local HTTP and insecure SQL are synthetic-lab conveniences. Access from a remote workstation should use an SSH tunnel; bank use requires approved TLS, identity, authorization and regional ingress.
gate: Gateway readiness and API routes work; only the gateway port is published; remote deployment runbook distinguishes tunnel access from production exposure.
